text:
Recent research cautions against interpreting rejection as a complete preference statement. [Vague Preference Policy Learning (2025)](https://research.ibm.com/publications/vague-preference-policy-learning-for-conversational-recommendation) shows that treating accepts/rejects as definitive can over-filter relevant alternatives. [PEPPER (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.1067/) identifies target-biased simulation and single-turn recall as weaknesses in conversational recommendation evaluation. Implication: annotate the reason actually expressed, preserving ambiguity rather than inferring hidden needs.

For ranking audits, [Rank-Preference Consistency (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.17097) motivates checking whether recommendation order respects preferences. Feedback format matters: [Peering Through Preferences (2024)](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/48a4f41ff000b121eabe7b2491b24aef-Abstract-Conference.html) finds substantial disagreement between rating-derived and pairwise preferences in LLM evaluation; this is adjacent evidence, not a recommender-specific result. For the twenty users, a defensible proposed audit would count rank inversions only when recorded feedback explicitly supports preferring one identified item over another. Rejection alone does not establish that pairwise ordering.

Drawing on [annotation quality management research (2024)](https://aclanthology.org/2024.cl-3.1/), independently annotate records before adjudication, report raw agreement and chance-corrected agreement, and retain disagreements. Proposed annotation fields: user/item ID, original rank, feedback evidence span, reason label, supporting catalog text, and evidence sufficiency. Distinguish specific-match rejection, reported duplication, and reported compatibility concern from independently verified facts. Abstain when identity or attributes are insufficient; report annotation coverage alongside agreement. These are proposed audit procedures, not measured findings about the twenty users; unavailable reviews, ratings, attributes, or simulator traits cannot support labels.
